newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Tung postpones U.S. visit.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Tung postpones U.S. visit.

text.p: Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa on Wednesday postponed plans to visit the United States until after the territory reverts to China in July.

Tung, appointed by China in December to run Hong Kong after Beijing resumes sovereignty, had originally planned to make a pre-handover trip to the United States to soothe fears there about the changeover.
"The Chief Executive believes his focus must be in Hong Kong," Tung said in a statement faxed to media.
A spokesman from his office said Tung attached great importance to Hong Kong's relationship with Washington and he would try to make a visit by the end of this year.

He denied the postponement was linked to a current visit to the United States by Martin Lee, leader of the popular Hong Kong Democratic Party, who is meeting President Bill Clinton at the end of the week.
"He (Tung) is just too busy," the spokesman said.
Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule on July 1 after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.

Lee has become a media star in the United States, where he has been been warning Washington about China's plan to curb political liberties and install a handpicked legislature to replace the elected lawmaking body when the flag is changed.
The spokesman said Tung was likely to go to the United States in the last quarter of the year, schedule permitting.
